batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 candidate IDs and their supplied packet predictions before measurement. Combine targeted follow-up of recent failures with matched solvent-response experiments, loading contrasts, and exploration of poorly measured condition regions of known scaffolds. Use one deliberate condition replicate to investigate heterogeneous evidence; do not rank acquisition value by predicted retention or raw quantile width.

choices.reason: Measure m125 at 0/1, 50 uL sample, and 300 uL DCM. The recent 2/1 observations 5c2bc1d92128a17d996d and cc2a23d8eb9de61d2ab3 showed a large completion difference with loading-solvent volume. This supplies the strong-eluent anchor for a matched test of that association's limits.

Pair the preceding m125 condition with 500 uL DCM. Both predictions are approximately 4/10 mL despite the repeated completion differences at 1/1 and 2/1. This tests whether the solvent-volume association disappears under pure EA or remains missing from the predictor.

Phenylmalonate at 20/1 and 100 uL fills an intermediate loading between the measured 10/1 anchors and e35fdc08a1113b193889 at 20/1, 150 uL. It helps constrain the moderate-to-weak response after 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e unexpectedly gave only 5.55/11.63 mL at 50/1 and lower loading.

Deliberately repeat the recorded phenylmalonate conditions of e35fdc08a1113b193889: 20/1 and 150 uL. An independent label tests reproducibility of its 15.84/31.84 mL anchor and helps interpret the unusual 50/1 result. This is condition replication, not a new condition, and cannot by itself establish a reproducible 50/1 reversal.

2-Phenylpyridine at 5/1 and 150 uL starts a matched moderate-ratio pair. Compare with lower-loading 292e0342682192a69fce and the large loading-dependent weak-eluent difference between 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 and 449b809e4efaaf2af86a. It tests where loading sensitivity becomes evident.

Complete the 2-phenylpyridine pair at 10/1 and 150 uL. The same-loading 5/1 comparison and lower-loading d119d77f545c029deace distinguish moderate-ratio response from the exceptional 50/1 behavior. The recent weak-eluent failure does not establish the response at this loading.

Acetophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL provides a loading contrast to recent 98020153aa4fb9db9b52, whose onset was historically underpredicted by 3.51 mL. Paired with the selected 20/1 condition, it supervises onset curvature in a common aromatic-ketone scaffold.

Add acetophenone at 20/1 and 100 uL. Recent 79aff1183a902fa3fb7e measured 16.96/25.17 mL at 50 uL, while 1d9eabd939a185c1b128 supplies a 100 uL, 50/1 anchor. This completes a useful fixed-loading ratio bridge and tests whether onset underprediction transfers across loading.

p-Methylacetophenone at 5/1 and 150 uL completes the loading series with 6e1413072d0468278d36 and 6a0f32348abbc91f704c. Their completion volumes are similar, whereas the 2/1 series includes substantially broader completion at high loading in 05a6276f67b3cca8cc7f. Test a ratio-dependent loading association.

o-Methoxyacetophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL supplies a less extreme anchor near b0a156972380db9bb945 at higher loading. Recent 52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b constrained the 50/1 low-loading response, but a3ae677aae8a8faf5786 remains an unusual 100 uL endpoint. This tests transfer of its onset behavior to an intermediate ratio.

Ethyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 100 uL tests whether the substantial response newly measured in 3c041f5186a291c3b313 at 50 uL persists at another loading. Together with f50c45b31cf41304c109 at 5/1, it separates loading-related onset changes from completion growth.

Extend that ethyl-acetoacetate series to 20/1 at the same 100 uL loading. Comparison with ac81adfab5ec8ce768db at 50 uL and the selected 10/1 label tests whether the onset and completion slopes transfer across loading, rather than simply increasing every beta-ketoester prediction.

Dibenzalacetone at 20/1 and 100 uL bridges 9f450a70d44f4384353f at 5/1 and c9bef93a79964dc6ede1 at 50/1. Its measured weak-eluent completion is much longer than chalcone's in 683b6279a87805548c7c. The intermediate label tests how conjugation topology changes the two endpoint curves.

2,6-Difluorobenzaldehyde at 5/1 and 50 uL establishes a nonzero-ratio baseline for sparse supplied coverage, including abcfcb23dbe2574a2389 at 0/1. It makes the selected 20/1 and 50/1 labels interpretable as a fixed-loading response curve.

Measure the same difluoroaldehyde at 20/1 and 50 uL. Its predicted completion near 30.57 mL is an untested transfer from other aldehydes. Comparison with the selected 5/1 and 50/1 points tests whether neighboring fluorines produce a different response shape from the dibromo environment represented by a30747adbe75d3a82d4f.

Complete the difluoroaldehyde curve at 50/1 and 50 uL. The predicted 11.30/37.90 mL is appreciably later than the measured weak-eluent dibromoaldehyde and bromochloroaldehyde anchors a30747adbe75d3a82d4f and 2eba456ca9391c3e3799. Test that structural transfer directly without treating the prediction as a finding.

The chloroethyl aryl ketone m170 at 10/1 and 100 uL fills a gap before fb3a6d49af84f3dc68c3 at 20/1. Pair it with the selected 50/1 condition to learn whether retention develops through onset delay, completion growth, or both in this side-chain environment.

Extend m170 to 50/1 at the same loading. Related chloroalkyl ketone m169 has comparatively early onset but long completion in f46da3c00b2199795e4c, while aliphatic m27 is much less retained in a3c1a0ac40733e8650fb. This label tests transfer across carbonyl placement and chain topology.

The benzylic cyclopropyl ketone m172 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends fd11ee7c408d95a1a8e6 at 20/1, which historically underpredicted completion by 5.82 mL. It tests whether the model captures the weak-eluent slope for a carbonyl environment distinct from directly aryl-conjugated ketones.

Cyclohexyl phenyl ketone at 50/1 and 50 uL explores an unmeasured weak-eluent region beyond strong-eluent 44601c22cc7d6f0f7e2e. The modest prediction tests transfer from the branched aryl ketone measured in f7bbba9684bf7983ccbf, rather than assuming every aromatic ketone develops late onset.

Salicylaldehyde at 1/1 and 100 uL begins a strong-to-moderate-eluent curve. Measured ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3 and 454eb2207b9abc0b2a6d already show broad completion at 0/1 and 2/1. This label tests whether the predictor's elevated 1/1 completion is warranted.

Measure salicylaldehyde at 5/1 with identical loading. The predictor gives earlier completion here than at 1/1, an untested trough rather than a chemical rule. The pair tests that ordering against the broad strong-eluent evidence and can improve endpoint-specific fitting for neighboring donor/carbonyl groups.

Add salicylaldehyde at 10/1 and 100 uL to locate recovery from the predicted completion trough. Together with the selected 1/1 and 5/1 points and weaker-eluent observations 8de30a7f5764c20b232e and d7b688cd2da99329d657, it tests curve shape while acknowledging loading differences at the latter anchors.

Bromosalicylaldehyde m186 at 10/1 and 100 uL fills the gap between its 2/1 and 20/1 coverage, including 5f1ae4e354b8b36ec691. Pair it with m190 at the same sample loading volume, while recognizing their different recorded densities and loading-solvent volumes.

The positional bromosalicylaldehyde m190 at 10/1 and 100 uL complements the selected m186 condition and measured d1774335b45258bc173a at 20/1. Their similar current endpoint predictions test whether positional transfer is adequate; the labels do not isolate substitution causally because recorded loading conditions also differ.

Bromobenzofuran at 50/1 and 100 uL checks loading transfer after recent 1525a3663c8d039331ed and 19e5d078bc0eb8a91e1e showed almost unchanged 10/1-to-50/1 endpoints at 50 uL. One cross-loading label tests whether that corrected flat response generalizes beyond the measured low-loading pair.

Acetophenone oxime at 0/1 and 150 uL tests a strong-eluent region without a supplied measured anchor. Its predicted completion exceeds the same-loading 2/1 prediction, despite stronger mobile phase. The label constrains whether donor-containing oxime broadening is already present under pure EA.

Measure the oxime at 1/1 and 100 uL. Observations 1182373ab8814dbe2f43 and 6b5982c6e1bbaadd6a95 anchor 5/1 and 10/1 at this loading, while 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f shows much later weak-eluent completion. This helps distinguish a strong-eluent completion minimum from a generic donor correction.

Nitrophenethyl alcohol at 1/1 and 50 uL tests whether the onset-loading association newly established at 2/1 persists at stronger eluent. Compare with a92f7617b135de150588 at the same loading and 5da8c25a3982216fb112 at 1/1, 150 uL. This separates onset sensitivity from its already long completion.

Ethyl p-aminobenzoate at 2/1 and 150 uL extends lower-loading d7f5057912ffbf1231a3 and connects to 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb at 5/1. Its predicted loading insensitivity can be tested against the onset decrease across the measured 5/1 loading series, without transferring the pyridine response to an aniline ester.

p-Methoxyphenethyl alcohol at 1/1 and 150 uL supplies a stronger-eluent anchor for the substantial 5/1 retention in e6e78489d1da4066c07e. It tests where this donor/ether scaffold's response develops and improves transfer relative to the distinct nitroalcohol completion behavior.

Measure p-methoxyphenethyl alcohol at 2/1 and 50 uL, comparing directly with 17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec at 100 uL and with nitroalcohol a92f7617b135de150588 at the same ratio and sample volume. This tests whether the pronounced nitroalcohol onset-loading association extends to a different phenethyl-alcohol substitution context.

hypotheses.content: For m125, larger recorded DCM loading-solvent volume is repeatedly associated with later completion at 1/1 and 2/1. The onset association is less consistent, and persistence under pure EA remains unknown. This is a conditional association, not an established solvent-volume mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The recent labels reveal a repeatable completion contrast that was almost absent from acquisition predictions. Measuring its strong-eluent boundary can teach an interaction instead of spreading a constant solvent-volume correction across ratios.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 50 uL sample loading under 0/1, do 300 and 500 uL DCM still produce different completion volumes?

hypotheses.content: Ester weak-eluent responses depend strongly on topology. Beta-ketoester completion growth does not transfer uniformly to malonate or acetylenic diesters; the recent low phenylmalonate 50/1 result leaves its local response and reproducibility unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched ethyl-acetoacetate ratios can improve conditional slopes, while a phenylmalonate loading extension and deliberate replicate constrain how unusual labels should influence related acceptor-rich structures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does ethyl acetoacetate reproduce its 10/1-to-20/1 growth at 100 uL, and is phenylmalonate's measured 20/1 anchor reproducible across an independent label and intermediate loading?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing scaffolds have distinct onset and completion responses conditioned on neighboring functional groups and loading. Broad completion can occur under strong eluent, while model-predicted strong-eluent troughs for salicylaldehyde and oxime remain untested. Nitroalcohol onset decreases across the measured 2/1 loading series.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These experiments distinguish early broad completion, delayed onset, and ratio-dependent loading associations. They can prevent a single donor-based correction from being transferred across phenols, oximes, and substituted phenethyl alcohols.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted salicylaldehyde and oxime strong-eluent response shapes reproducible, and does the nitroalcohol loading association persist at 1/1 or extend to the methoxyphenethyl-alcohol context?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic and related carbonyl response curves require local structural and endpoint-specific conditioning. Loading associations differ between ordinary ketones, and weak-eluent transfer remains insufficiently tested for several halogenated aldehydes and side-chain carbonyl environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Common acetophenone conditions offer broad Row relevance, while connected difluoroaldehyde and chloroethyl-ketone curves test structural transfer where measured ratio coverage is sparse. Moderate-retention ketones also constrain overgeneralization from long intervals.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do acetophenone onset corrections transfer across loading, does p-methylacetophenone retain its 2/1 completion-loading association at 5/1, and are the predicted weak-eluent curves of the less covered carbonyl environments accurate?

hypotheses.content: Basic heteroaromatic weak-eluent growth can involve both endpoints, and its loading dependence is scaffold- and ratio-dependent. The lower-loading 2-phenylpyridine onset decrease from 20/1 to 50/1 does not generalize to the newly measured 100 uL pair.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The recent 100 uL weak-eluent failure argues against treating nitrogen-associated broadening as completion-only or assuming a common onset-loading trend. Moderate-ratio labels at another loading can locate where response shapes begin to differ.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, how do the 5/1 and 10/1 endpoints compare with the measured 50 uL curve, and does loading sensitivity already appear before the weak-eluent regime?

feedback_interpretation: The m125 experiment strengthened a specific completion association: at 2/1, V2 was 29.49 versus 63.99 mL at 50 uL and 31.38 versus 69.81 mL at 150 uL for 300 versus 500 uL DCM. The 100 uL onset remains exceptional, so I narrowed the interpretation to a repeatable completion association and selected its pure-EA boundary. Neutral m4 now shows increasing 50/1 completion across loading, 18.77, 22.45, and 24.04 mL, whereas m33's 5/1 loading pair was nearly stable. This weakens any universal loading correction. The p-methylacetophenone midpoint supports a larger high-loading completion change at 2/1 than is yet established at 5/1. Acetophenone's new intermediate onsets were historically underpredicted, motivating cross-loading anchors in this common family. The phenolic intermediates locate substantial m58 response growth beyond 20/1, while m209 confirms long weak-eluent completion. Nitroalcohol now has a coherent 2/1 onset decrease with increasing loading, motivating a stronger-eluent and structural comparison. The 2-phenylpyridine 100 uL pair changed the earlier endpoint-asymmetry hypothesis: both onset and completion increased strongly toward 50/1, unlike the lower-loading onset ordering. Phenylmalonate's low 50/1 label and bromobenzofuran's nearly flat low-loading ratio pair weaken generic weak-eluent growth assumptions; I follow the former with a controlled extension and replicate and the latter with only one loading-transfer check. Ethyl acetoacetate's new 10/1 underprediction supports another loading-specific ratio bridge, while the relatively accurate cyclic-ester 20/1 result reduces the urgency of further similar interpolation. These are acquisition-time errors; retraining has changed the predictor, so none is assumed to remain a current residual.
batch_rationale: The batch uses connected labels to address relationships shared across the Row-distribution. Two m125 conditions test whether a newly supported loading-solvent-volume association depends on mobile-phase strength. Acetophenone, p-methylacetophenone, ethyl acetoacetate, and 2-phenylpyridine receive loading or ratio contrasts that can distinguish conditional endpoint responses from an averaged correction. The phenylmalonate replicate is a deliberate use of an eligible duplicate condition to assess reproducibility of an anchor implicated by surprising neighboring evidence; it is paired with a new loading condition. A three-point difluoroaldehyde curve and a matched chloroethyl-ketone pair explore poorly measured structure-condition regions, with related measured carbonyls providing transfer references. Salicylaldehyde's three-point series tests a concrete predicted trough, and complementary oxime, bromophenol-aldehyde, nitroalcohol, aminoester, and methoxyphenethyl-alcohol measurements examine whether similar functional-group counts conceal different onset and completion relationships. Modest predicted-retention ketones and the bromobenzofuran loading check constrain excessive transfer from long-retention failures. Raw quantile widths are secondary evidence: many supplied V2 lower quantiles are zero, and some quantiles cross, so width alone is not a reliable information-gain measure. The batch targets learnable recorded-condition associations and useful supervision where variation remains unexplained, without assigning mechanisms to absent experimental variables or optimizing the selected chromatographic outcomes.
